conviction_note: Mild long lean: Medifast has set wide quarterly guides and beaten the EPS end of them twice running (Q2 -0.28 against a -0.50 to -1.00 guide; stock +34% and +22% on the last two prints), and consensus EPS of -0.60 sits at the bottom of the -0.15 to -0.65 Q3 guide. Against that, Q3 is seasonally the weakest quarter (2025 Q2 to Q3 revenue -15%) and the coach count is still falling, so revenue near or slightly under the $69.2m consensus is plausible. abs_move 10 (the name's last two reactions were 22-34% and the ATM IV of 58.6% implies a roughly 15% event move on an unusable chain), p_up 57, giving +1.4. Findings sum to +1.8 because the per-finding sizes and the scaled number are separate measurements; the scaled number is smaller because the revenue risk and the reduced short fuel pull p_up toward 50. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue (-1.5%); on EPS I expect a beat of roughly 0.2-0.3 per share against -0.60.
bar: Company guide (Q2 8-K, 2026-08-03): Q3 revenue $60-80m, loss per share $0.15-0.65 excluding one-time Catalyst costs; FY26 revenue $270-300m, loss per share $0.25-1.75 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm). Consensus Q3 EPS -0.60 and revenue $69.18m (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/MED). A second source gives EPS -0.62 and revenue $67.7m from a single estimate as of 2026-08-03 (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/medifast-hebt-fy26-eps-ausblick-trotz-verlust-q2-zeigt-coach-wende-q3-umsatzband-setzt-erwartungen). The two EPS estimates agree within $0.02, and the company guide is primary, so the bar counts as sourced. The consensus covers about three analysts.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest at the 2026-09-30 settlement: 1,053,225 shares, 9.78% of float, 7.3 days to cover, down 43% from 1,862,070 at 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/MED/short-interest/, published 2026-10-09; Equibles agrees, https://equibles.com/stocks/med/shortinterest). The peak was about 2.18m in late May 2026. At the current 20-day average volume of 106.6k shares, days to cover is about 10. No usable skew: the baseline chain is unusable (ATM spread 86% of mid, skew null). Put/call OI ratio is 0.24 and ATM IV is 58.6% on the 2026-11-20 expiry. Turnover is thin, about $1.3m a day. Spot of $11.79 is 24.8% above the 52-week low and 10.3% below the 52-week high, with a 20-day run-up of -3.1%.

findings.finding: The company sandbags its EPS guide and consensus sits at the bottom of it. Q2 2026 printed -$0.28 against its own -$0.50 to -$1.00 guide, above the top of the range. Q1 2026 printed -$0.19 against roughly -$0.53 consensus, about -$0.39 excluding a $2.2m one-time facility-sale gain. Q3 consensus is -$0.60 against a guide the company improved to -$0.15 to -$0.65 (ex-Catalyst), so a print anywhere above the bottom tenth of the range beats.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints were large EPS beats against sandbagged guides and were bought: 2026-08-03 +34.29% and 2026-05-04 +22.48% (baseline). Earlier prints with small beats or misses moved -0.8% to +0.8%, and -11.4% in Feb 2025.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected the pattern to repeat, consensus would sit near the -0.40 midpoint rather than at -0.60, and the stock would not have given back about 10% from its post-Q2 high. The 20-day run-up is -3.1%, not a pre-print rally. Partly priced: the beat pattern is public, and the landing is inside the guided range unless it clears -0.15.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 8-K: Q2 guide -0.50 to -1.00 and the $2.2m Ridgely sale gain in Q1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026029812/medq12026earningsrelease.htm; Q2 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051928/med-20260630.htm). Consensus from EarningsWhispers (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/MED). On the Q2 call the CFO said the EPS range 'has actually gotten better' (https://www.webull.com/news/15381704353604608).

findings.finding: Q3 is Medifast's seasonally weakest quarter and the coach base is still shrinking. In 2025 revenue went from $105.6m in Q2 to $89.4m in Q3 (-15.3%) and coaches from 22,800 to 19,500 (-14.5%), with revenue per coach flat ($4,630 to $4,585). In 2026 coaches fell from 14,000 in Q1 to 11,700 in Q2 (-16%) and management guided further declines. Applying 2025's Q2-to-Q3 seasonality to $76.4m gives about $65m, below the $69.2m consensus and the $70m midpoint. Offset: revenue per coach rose 20% sequentially in Q2, and the new comp plan (Aug 1) and Trilivy Reset launch (July) could lift it again.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue misses of a few hundred thousand dollars barely moved the stock: Q3 2025 missed by about $0.3m and the stock moved +0.84%. The stock has traded on EPS and the path to profitability, not on revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $69.2m sits just under the $70m guide midpoint, as if Q3 2026 will be down only about 9% sequentially against 15% a year earlier. If the seasonality were priced, revenue consensus would be nearer $65m. This is an inference from the company's own prior-year pattern, not a datum about Q3 2026.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 2026 8-K with finding 1 for the 11,700 coaches and $76.4m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm). The CFO said on the Q2 call that coach counts will decline in the short term (https://www.webull.com/news/15381704353604608). There is no independent Q3 2026 demand series: no web-traffic, app or Reddit data was found.

findings.finding: On the 2026-08-03 call the CFO said Catalyst cost savings ('millions of dollars of savings') could not yet be quantified and 'we are going to be doing that in our Q3 earnings call'. With the Q4 2026 return-to-profitability target and a director from the activist Steamboat, who pushed for cost cuts, now on the board, this print should deliver the first quantified savings number and a test of the Q4 profit commitment.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 print, which raised the FY EPS range from -1.55/-2.75 to -0.25/-1.75 and promised Q4 profitability, was bought +34.3%. No prior quantified-savings disclosure exists to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: The dollar figure does not exist in public yet, and consensus FY EPS (-1.85 per Goldesel) sits below the low end of the company's -1.75 FY guide, which says analysts do not credit the savings. If they did, FY consensus would sit near the -1.0 midpoint. Risk: one-time Catalyst charges will hit GAAP Q3 and could make the headline look worse.
findings.independence: Steamboat's March 2026 letter asks for 'thoughtful cost-cutting and right-sizing' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910329/000121390026032212/ea028275401ex99-2.htm). The Q2 8-K says most Catalyst execution falls in Q3 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm).

findings.finding: Balance-sheet floor and insider buying. At $11.79 on 11.18m shares the market cap is about $132m, against $169.8m of cash and investments with no debt at 2026-06-30, and the CFO expects working capital above $145m at year-end. Director Parsa Kiai (Steamboat) bought about 131k shares at $11.60-12.26 on 2026-08-19/20/24/26, taking the stake to 790,693 shares (7.1%). 1,323,568 shares remain on the buyback authorization, unused in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock has traded below net cash since early 2025, per Steamboat. A below-cash valuation did not stop the -11.4% reaction in Feb 2025, but the last two prints rebounded hard from near cash value.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the filings are public. What it adds is asymmetry, because a miss is cushioned by about $15 a share of cash. If the market feared a cash burn, the stock would trade well below cash rather than at about 0.8x.
findings.independence: Form 4s filed 2026-08-26 and 2026-08-28 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/910329/000121390026094862/0001213900-26-094862.txt). The 10-Q shows the cash, investments and buyback authorization (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051928/med-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest fell 43% in the second half of September, from 1,862,070 shares at the 2026-09-15 settlement to 1,053,225 (9.8% of float, 7.3 days to cover) at 2026-09-30. Much less squeeze fuel is in place than before the +22% and +34% prints, when about 2m shares were short (17-20% of float).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two upside reactions came with short interest near 1.8-2.2m shares. No print has yet come with short interest near 1m.
findings.why_not_priced: The figure is public. What it changes is the magnitude of an upside reaction rather than the sign. The cover itself (about 800k shares, roughly seven days of volume) may also mean an informed short stood down before the print, which is ambiguous.
findings.independence: Equibles shows the same settlement figures and a model estimate of about 1.0m for 2026-10-15 (https://equibles.com/stocks/med/shortinterest).

findings.finding: Director and former CEO Daniel Chard sold 19,089 shares under a 10b5-1 plan on 2026-09-28/29 at about $11.73-11.98, roughly 5% of his direct and indirect holdings.
findings.why_not_priced: Small, public and pre-arranged, so it is near zero by design. It is filed for breadth because it is the only insider sale near the print.
findings.independence: Form 144s filed 2026-09-28/29 (EDGAR filing index for CIK 910329).

findings.finding: GLP-1 competition has widened in 2026. Oral orforglipron was approved 2026-04-01 at $149/month on LillyDirect, and Truveta data to 2026-07-06 show 40.3% of initiators were GLP-1-naive, adding to the client-acquisition pressure Medifast names as its main headwind.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Medifast has cited GLP-1 adoption in every release since 2024. The Q2 2026 print, the first full quarter with orforglipron, was bought +34%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since Q2 already included April-June. This is a macro proxy the company has not quantified for Q3.
findings.independence: Proxy. The company names GLP-1 adoption as the cause of coach declines (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000910329/000162828026051845/medq22026earningsrelease.htm).

findings.finding: The Q3 release moves from after the close (every print in the baseline was amc, including Q2 on 2026-08-03 with a 4:30 pm call) to before the open on Monday 2026-10-26, with an 8:30 am ET call, per a relay of the company's announcement. The whole reaction therefore lands in one regular session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No bmo print in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: No directional content. It is filed so the judges know the timing changed. Some calendars (AJ Bell, StockAnalysis) still show Nov 3/5, so part of the market may not expect the print on Monday.
findings.independence: Sweep row session evidence. AJ Bell lists 2026-11-03 (https://www.ajbell.co.uk/market-research/sub/NYSE:MED/company-info), which conflicts.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew. The lean agrees with the name's own recent reaction history (two big beats bought) and against the -3.1% 20-day drift, which is mild, so nothing in the baseline argues strongly against a modest long.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (a finding inside the guided range): trimmed finding 1, the EPS-beat pattern, from +2.5 to +2.0, because most of the plausible landing zone lies inside the company's own -0.15 to -0.65 guide.
Rules 1 and 8 checked, no change: the reaction history shows beats on this line bought (+22%, +34%), so no veto, and thin coverage keeps abs_move_pct at 10.
Rule 5 checked, no change: the GLP-1 proxy was already filed small (-0.5), and the seasonality finding rests on the company's own prior-year numbers rather than an outside series.
Rule 7 checked: short interest was looked up before the negative findings, and at 9.8% of float it is not crowded, so the negatives were not shrunk.
